chunks: Zurārah narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام:

That the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, when he returned from ʿArafāt and proceeded to Minā, entered the mosque. The people gathered around him asking him about Laylat al-Qadr, so he stood as a preacher and spoke after praising Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

As for what follows, you asked me about Laylat al-Qadr, and I did not conceal it from you because I knew it; rather, I was not knowledgeable of it. Know, O people, that whoever reaches the month of Ramaḍān while sound and healthy, then fasts its days, stands in worship for a portion of its nights, remains constant in his salat, goes forth to his Friday prayer, and goes out to his Eid, then he has attained Laylat al-Qadr and won the prize of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.بِجَائِزَةِ الرَّبِّ: The reward or prize granted by the Lord
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramaḍān, the sacred month of fasting
key_terms.عِيدِهِ: His Eid prayer or attendance at Eid
key_terms.فَصَامَ نَهَارَهُ: He fasted its days, meaning he observed the daytime fasts of Ramaḍān
key_terms.قَامَ وِرْدًا مِنْ لَيْلِهِ: He stood in worship for a portion of its night
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Decree, the blessed night sought in Ramaḍān
key_terms.وَاظَبَ عَلَى صَلَاتِهِ: He remained constant in his prescribed salat

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe attaining Laylat al-Qadr through the worship of Ramaḍān?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم answering a question about Laylat al-Qadr after returning from ʿArafāt. It teaches that the one who fully observes the acts of worship of Ramaḍān—fasting, night worship, regular salat, Jumuʿah, and Eid prayer—has attained the blessing of Laylat al-Qadr and the reward of Allah.
